summary: A 1980 suggestion that systems install mail address synonyms for official roles, such as SYSTEMS or MANAGEMENT, so mail reaches whoever holds the job. It also suggests the NIC pick a standard set.

eli5.summary: Write to the Principal not to a person, and it reaches whoever has the job today. This note suggests that for email.

subtitle: Use role-based mail addresses so messages reach the current job holder, not a specific person.

tldr.problem: When mail is sent to a person by name and that person moves to a different role or organization, the mail becomes undeliverable unless they update their correspondents.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 763 suggests creating mail address synonyms for official roles (SYSTEMS, MANAGEMENT, LIAISON) that map to the current job holder, regardless of changes in personnel.
tldr.outcome: This is a brief suggestion, not a standard. The concept of role-based addresses has been useful in organizations, though email-based role handling varies widely.

today: RFC 763 is a simple suggestion, not a standard. Modern organizations often create role-based distribution lists or mailboxes, though these are typically implemented through mailing list systems or directory services rather than simple address synonyms.

sections.title: The Problem of Employee Turnover
sections.content: In large organizations, mail often needs to reach someone in a particular role rather than a specific individual. When the person in a role changes due to resignations, promotions, or reassignments, mail sent to their personal address becomes undeliverable. This happens frequently in organizations like NBS (National Bureau of Standards).
sections.eli5: When the manager quits, mail to their email address bounces. You have to figure out who the new manager is and resend it.

sections.title: Role-Based Mail Address Synonyms
sections.content: RFC 763 recommends that mail systems supporting address synonyms install common role mailboxes such as SYSTEMS, MANAGEMENT, and LIAISON. These addresses are mapped to the current job holder through the system's mail address forwarding mechanism. When someone leaves a role, the mapping is updated to point to the new incumbent, without changing the role address itself.
sections.eli5: The address SYSTEMS always goes to whoever manages the computers, even if that person changes.

sections.title: Standardization and Adoption
sections.content: The RFC proposes that the NIC (Network Information Center) or ARPANET management select and publish a standardized set of role mailboxes that all sites should support. This would increase the utility of role-based addressing across the entire network. However, RFC 763 is a brief memo, not a specification, leaving the details of implementation to individual systems.
sections.eli5: If every site used the same role names, mail to SYSTEMS@anywhere would go to the right person everywhere.
